inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 fix the same leak (wallet rebroadcast bypassing -privatebroadcast) with opposite approaches: #34533 routes rebroadcasts through private broadcast, #36330 suppresses them. They cannot both land; review #34533 first since it preserves rebroadcast liveness, then decide.
#35558 is stacked on #35724; the logging/accounting PR must be reviewed and landed first even though its standalone value is low.

Orphan/1p1c chain: #36437 (reconsideration reassignment + invariant harness), #36369 (same-txid variant cancellations, which unblocks #36371 outside this list), and #36486 (non-witness parent request retention) all touch the same orphanage/1p1c paths. Review order #36437 -> #36369 -> #36486.

Three overlapping cs_main reduction efforts: #36244 (async block processing), #36445 (skip cs_main with no orphan work) and #35561 (CNodeState fields to Peer). #36445 is the smallest independent slice and should be reviewed first; #36244 likely subsumes parts of the others.

#35502 and #35522 are the same kind of move-only net_processing extraction but were banded differently when assessed alone; now both P4. #35522 arose from review of #34824, so #34824 should be reviewed first.

Private broadcast cluster all builds on merged #29415: #34271 (make the tracker optional) conflicts structurally with #34322 (persistence) and #36477 (reporting finished txs). #34271 should land last or be rebased on whichever of the other two lands.

#30988 (SockMan split) and #35040 (LocalAddressManager) are both parts of the net/net_processing split (#33958 / #30694); #30988 is foundational and should be reviewed before the dependent extractions.

Three addrman changes touch selection/insertion: #36449 (uniform in-bucket sampling), #33663 (filter during selection), #36208 (time penalty in nTime check). #36449 is the most consequential and will likely conflict with #33663; review it first.

Four Tor-related changes (#36142, #36170, #36177, #36374) touch torcontrol and proxy/network parsing; they overlap textually and should be reviewed as a group. #36170 additionally breaks existing -bind setups at startup, so its compatibility decision gates the others.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small P1 set of remotely-triggerable memory/liveness defects, a broad P2 band of relay-correctness, addrman-quality, DoS-bypass and privacy fixes, a long P3 tail of edge-case fixes, opt-in operator features, net_processing refactors and test-coverage repairs, and a handful of P4 janitorial moves. Two adjustments dominate: addrman and headers-sync correctness fixes were under-placed when assessed alone and have been pulled to the top of P2, while opt-in private-broadcast work (a new, user-enabled feature) was over-placed and now sits in the middle of P2. Eight of the test PRs fix vacuously-passing assertions rather than adding new coverage; they are genuinely worth review but none of them should displace P2 work.
